extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural researchers, applicants, institutional research administrators, and other stakeholders in NIH grant funding
extracted.subtask_description: A news/updates page summarizing policy changes, resources, and reminders relevant to preparing NIH grant applications and understanding review/award processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate research models
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches and encourages those that enhance human relevance and translational potential. Choose models that best address the hypothesis and research aims rather than selecting models solely because they are fashionable or familiar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow PF5 Collaborative International Research Project application format
rubrics_metrics.description: Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must use the PF5 application format and be aware that applications may be administratively split into linked awards after peer review and before Just-in-Time. Review the overview video/resource to ensure compliance with format and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: A new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format is available based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS Plans for applicable submissions, use the issued 2026 Pilot format and include the simplified required elements specified in that format. Consult the resource to ensure the plan meets NIH requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address replication and reproducibility in applications and awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Embedding Replication and Reproducibility Throughout NIH Research: key reminders for applications, awards, and a new Highlighted Topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan encourages a culture valuing replication and reproducibility. Applicants should consider and document how their work supports reliability (e.g., replication plans, reproducible methods, transparency of materials/data) and watch for related highlighted-topic funding opportunities and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand 'Competitive But Not Discussed' scoring implications
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH implemented emergency modifications designating the middle third of applications in a study section as “competitive but not discussed.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut-off for discussion; being scored as 'competitive but not discussed' reflects these procedural review designations following the resumption of activities after a funding lapse. Applicants should interpret review outcomes with this context in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult the NIH Data Book for up-to-date fiscal and program data
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore the NIH Data Book — fiscal year updates are being rolled out to provide the most recent information available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the NIH Data Book as a resource for current fiscal year data and trends that may inform application strategy, institutional planning, and understanding of funding patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of NIH small business program changes (Seed Fund)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH’s Seed Fund (Small Business Program) has been reinstated, affecting innovators, founders, and R&D-driven small companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small business applicants and tech transfer offices should note program availability, eligibility, and timelines associated with the Seed Fund when preparing SBIR/STTR or other small-business-directed proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for effects of centralized peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Centralization of NIH peer review within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) aims to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware that consolidation of peer review may change study section composition, review procedures, and potentially competitive dynamics; review-related guidance and notices (e.g., NIH Guide Notices) describe these changes and implications for submissions.
